newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares extend gains but plateau seen ahead.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares extend gains but plateau seen ahead.

text.p: Delhi shares opened higher on Wednesday on purchases of blue chips by domestic and foreign investors, but brokers said they expected the market to begin cooling off after a recent rally.
The Delhi bourse's sensitive index was up 3.93 points at 961.48 at the end of 30 minutes of trade.

The sensitive index jumped 2.8 percent on Monday at the start of a new settlement period, and surged another 2.2 percent on Tuesday after Hindustan Lever Ltd announced a 39 percent rise in net profit in the first six months of 1997.
"At this level, the market should see some resistance as profit-takers might start selling at current higher levels," said Ajay Kapoor of brokerage Radha Kishan.
ITC Ltd increased three rupees to 583.50.
Reliance Industries gained 0.75 rupee to 375.50 on selective buying by speculators.
State Bank of India quoted 2.25 rupees higher at 341.50.
ACC was up seven rupees to 1,682, while TELCO rose 7.80 rupees to 407.
